text:
A patient may need a tracheostomy when the upper airway is blocked or when breathing support through a tube will be needed for a long time. The procedure opens the windpipe through the neck so air can reach the lungs, secretions can be cleared, and a tube does not have to stay through the mouth or nose. Common reasons include trauma, tumors, swelling, neurological illness that weakens breathing or swallowing, and difficulty weaning from a ventilator.
